chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Sama'ah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about raisins (dried grapes) in exchange for fresh grapes. He said, 'It is not valid except like for like.' He said, 'And fresh dates and dried dates [are exchanged] like for like.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging fresh dates for dried dates in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the exchange of fresh grapes for raisins or fresh dates for dried dates requires an equal measure and immediate hand-to-hand delivery to avoid *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange). This ruling extends the principle of *mithlan bi-mithl* to these specific foodstuffs, ensuring that the inherent moisture and weight differences do not introduce uncertainty (*gharar*) or usury in commercial transactions. The emphasis on 'like for like' underscores the Shia jurisprudential focus on preserving equity in trade by treating these items as equivalent commodities when their form changes but their essence remains.
